lesson.title: After Your Serve
lesson.hook: Your partner stays near the net. The return is coming towards your side of the baseline.
lesson.liveIntro: Your partner stays near the net. The return is coming towards your side of the baseline.

dhA.name: Where will you send this groundstroke?
dhA.sit: The return bounces deep on your serving side.
dhA.q: Where will you send this groundstroke?
opts: Use controlled depth through the middle

lines.A: You give the ball room and prepare together for another reply.
lines.B: It lands here, but the smaller target leaves less margin. Keep covering.

dhA.take: Partner holds. Keep covering your half.
dhA.payoff: Partner holds. Keep covering your half.
dhA.principle: Partner holds. Keep covering your half.
dhA.why: Switching is a response to your partner’s movement. Here they hold, so a blind switch leaves the return lane uncovered. Recover, split for the return and read the height you receive.

lesson.pairPlan: If you hold at the net, I keep my half. We switch when the movement calls for it, not automatically.
lesson.returnPrompt: Same partnership. Read what has changed.

comparison.summary: All four players stay involved. This is one illustrated continuation, not a predicted result.
comparison.intro: Same incoming ball. Compare how the first call changes the pair’s next job.

summaries.10: The pair’s first move fitted. The next contact still needed margin.
summaries.11: You read the pair’s coverage and gave the next ball room.
summaries.01: Your next shot had margin. Review the first coverage call together.

lesson.completionIntro: One call. Two responsibilities. Take the plan to your next match.

pro.label: The Bryans · The wide serve has a cost
pro.moment: In their interview with Mark Hodgkinson, the Bryan brothers gave a concrete example: when a partner serves wide, the net player needs to cover the line. The serve creates space for both teams. Their plan accounted for the reply, not just the delivery.
pro.read: Your next point: your partner holds here. Keep your own side covered and read the return; a switch needs a reason, not a habit.
pro.src: Bob & Mike Bryan · Interview with Mark Hodgkinson · Tennisplayer

drill.name: Rehearse as a pair
drill.how: Alternate agreed cross and hold signals before serving. Play the return. The server must cover the appropriate half without guessing from the previous point.
